expectation: Membrane ring on helper T cells (bright) and dim on monocytes/macrophages. In gut mucosa: common, scattered through the lamina propria in the villi, denser in lymphoid aggregates, sparse in the epithelium.
observed: A: yellow cells spread along the mucosa and lamina propria of both sections, not following the tissue outline. B/C: few cells, a few bright blobs (likely debris). D: a bright blob next to dimmer cells. E: crisp membrane rings that sit mostly on CD3E+ cells (white in the merge).
why: Membrane-ring CD4 cells overlap a subset of CD3E+ T cells in a lymphoid area and are spread through the lamina propria, as expected.
notes: CD4 shows clear membrane rings on a subset of CD3E+ T cells in a lymphoid area and is spread through the lamina propria. The brightest yellow blobs in B and E look like debris and were not used for the verdict.
